# SENTRY POST — BRICK MASONRY WALLS  ·  design change SP-B1
## Underground CBRN-hardened blast-resistant protective structure and sentry post — Pune, Maharashtra

**Works Management package revision WM1** · 07 September 2026
**Geometry:** Architectural Rev F · Structural Phase 2 Rev A + M1 · **Services:** Drainage DR1 · HVAC HV1 · Schedule of Finishes FN1 · Structural CAD SC1
**Evidence classes:** `[C]` confirmed · `[D]` derived here · `[A]` assumed by this package ·
`[U]` unresolved · `[N]` not available — data required

> **THE ONLY DESIGN CHANGE in this package is reference SP-B1: the sentry post walls
> are BRICK MASONRY, replacing the Rev F 200 mm RC ballistic infill panels.
> No other element of the project is changed.**

---

## The decision

The sentry post walls are BRICK MASONRY. This replaces the '200 RC BALLISTIC INFILL PANELS' shown on Rev F drawings 3, 4 and 6 and described in master A.4.8. It is the only design change carried by this Works Management package and it is recorded as reference SP-B1.

## What follows from it

Two consequences follow and are recorded rather than buried. First, brick masonry does not provide the ballistic protection that the Rev F panels were named for; the change removes a stated protective function from the sentry post, which is already a structure the project declares NOT blast designed and expendable. Second, the openings now need lintels, which the RC panels did not, and no lintel design exists anywhere in the project. Both are carried into the verification register for the designer to close.

### Why 190 mm and not 230 mm

The confirmed structural zone between the column faces is **200 mm** (master A.4.8:
external 4000 × 5000, internal 3600 × 4600, columns 350 × 350 with their outer faces
flush with the wall). Two standard Indian brick sizes are available:

* **Modular, IS 1077, 190 × 90 × 90** — builds a 190 mm one-brick wall, which fits
  inside the 200 mm zone with 10 mm to spare. The 10 mm is taken up at the internal
  face and absorbed in the plaster.
* **Conventional, 230 × 110 × 75** — builds a 230 mm wall, which would project 30 mm
  beyond the column faces and change the confirmed 4000 × 5000 external envelope.

The modular brick is adopted because it preserves every confirmed dimension. Using
the conventional brick would be a second design change, and the instruction for this
package is that there is only one.

### Why the panel height is 2.600 m

This is the project's **own confirmed figure**, not an assumption of this package.
Master A.7.7 gives the infill load on the first-floor beams as 13.000 kN/m and
verifies it as 0.200 × 2.600 × 25; Rev F drawing 6 repeats '200 × 2600 high'.

The first storey checks geometrically: roof slab top +6.700 less the 450 beam depth
gives a soffit at +6.250, and +6.250 − +3.650 = 2.600. **It agrees.**

The ground storey does not: first floor +3.650 less 450 gives a soffit at +3.200, and
+3.200 − +0.450 = **2.750**, which is 150 mm more than the project's own figure. The
confirmed 2.600 is used for both storeys and the 150 mm difference is carried as
verification item **WM-V1**. It is declared, not resolved.

## Construction method


**1. SOURCE APPROVAL AND TESTING.** Bricks are procured against IS 1077 as class designation 10 (10 N/mm² minimum average compressive strength). Samples are drawn to IS 5454 and tested to IS 3495 for compressive strength, water absorption, efflorescence and warpage before any brick is laid. On a military structure the source is approved once and not changed without retesting.

**2. STACKING AND WETTING.** Bricks are stacked to IS 4082 clear of the working area and are thoroughly soaked before laying so that they do not draw water out of the mortar. Dry bricks in a CM 1:6 bed are the most common cause of weak masonry on Indian sites.

**3. MORTAR.** Cement mortar 1:6 by volume for the general walling, prepared and used to IS 2250, with sand to IS 2116. Mortar is used within 30 minutes of mixing and is never re-tempered. Gauge boxes are used — proportioning by shovel is not accepted.

**4. BOND AND COURSING.** English bond, one brick thick. Joints are 10 mm and are fully filled — bed, cross and vertical. Every fourth course is checked for level and every panel is checked for plumb. Courses are kept level and no part of the wall is raised more than one metre above another in a day's work.

**5. INTERFACE WITH THE FRAME.** The masonry is an INFILL between RC columns and under RC beams. It is not a load-bearing wall and must not be built tight to the beam soffit in one operation: the top course is left down and is wedged and packed after the panel below has taken its initial shrinkage, so that the panel does not attract load from the frame it was not designed to carry.

**6. TIES TO THE COLUMNS.** The masonry is tied to the columns so that the panel is restrained out of plane. The tie detail does not exist in the project and is carried as a verification item; until it is designed, the assumption for planning is starter bars or proprietary ties at every fourth course.

**7. SEISMIC NOTE — NOT RESOLVED HERE.** Master A.7.8 records that the sentry post uses R = 3.0 precisely BECAUSE the infill is not separated from the frame, and B.8 designs to V_b = 73.18 kN. Substituting brick masonry at about 20 kN/m³ for 200 RC at 25 kN/m³ reduces the infill line load from 13.000 kN/m to roughly 9.9 kN/m and therefore reduces the seismic weight, which points the existing design in the conservative direction. That is a direction, not a verification. The structural discipline must re-run the check; this package does not.

**8. LINTELS.** RC lintels are required over D1, W1 and the eight vision panels. Bearing is taken as 200 each end for planning. NO LINTEL DESIGN EXISTS IN THE PROJECT — section, reinforcement and bearing are to be designed before the openings are built, and the 200 x 150 section used for the estimate is for quantity only.

**9. CURING.** Masonry is kept damp for at least seven days. Chases for electrical conduit are CUT, not hammered, and never cut into a course until the masonry has cured.

**10. TOLERANCES AND INSPECTION.** Line, level, plumb and joint thickness are inspected at a hold point at the end of each storey before plaster. Plumb over the 2.600 storey height and joint thickness are the two measurements that decide whether the plaster can be held to its stated thickness.

## Programme

| Activity | Description | Days | Predecessor logic |
|---|---|---:|---|
| `A1176` | Modular bricks — source approval, testing and order | 20 | After the quality plan is approved; **before** any brick is delivered |
| `A8130` | Brick delivery, stacking, sampling and testing to IS 3495 | 4 | After `A1176` and after the first-floor slab is cast |
| `A8135` | **Brick masonry — ground storey** | 5 | After the first-floor slab has cured (`A8090`) so there is something to build up to |
| `A8140` | RC lintels — ground storey | 2 | After `A8135` |
| `A8145` | **HOLD POINT** — line, level, plumb, joint thickness | 1 | After `A8135` and `A8140` |
| `A8150` | **Brick masonry — first storey** | 4 | After the roof has cured (`A8120`) and the ground storey is signed off |
| `A8155` | RC lintels — first storey | 2 | After `A8150` |
| `A8160` | **HOLD POINT** — first storey inspection | 1 | After `A8150` and `A8155` |
| `A8165` | **MILESTONE** — sentry post brick masonry complete | 0 | — |
| `A8175` | Electrical conduits and boxes **chased** into the masonry | 4 | After the masonry hold point — chases are cut, never hammered, and never before curing |
| `A8180` | Internal plaster 12 mm sand faced, CM 1:4 | 6 | After the electrical first fix |
| `A8185` | External plaster 15 mm, two coat, with scaffolding | 6 | After the internal plaster |

Each storey is built only after the slab above it has cured, so the masonry is built
into a completed frame rather than the frame being completed around it. The
alternative — building the masonry as the frame rises — would put the panel under
load from the frame's own deflection, which is exactly what the wedging rule exists
to prevent.
